correctness.rationale: For scalar a+bz, write H=|a|²+|b|² and r=2|a||b|/H; since maximal arc cosine A is at least maximal two-node cosine B, squared reconstruction ratio (1+rA)/(1+rB) increases in r, so extremizers may be balanced |a|=|b|. A peak phase eta∈[0,pi] has exact piecewise ratio sec(|eta-s|/2) for eta<=theta and cos((eta-theta)/2)/cos((eta-s)/2) otherwise; the latter is increasing, leading to three sharp terms. The first increases and third decreases in s and meet only at tan(s/2)=sin(theta/2); the second is subdominant at the crossing, giving the unique minimizer. Matrix-coefficient scalarization for A+zB with unit vectors proves every amplification is bounded by scalar norm, and n=1 attains equality. Independent angular-grid phase maxima across five arc widths and three node schedules confirmed profiles and optimizers; finite grids do not establish analytical all-parameter uniqueness or cb bound.
residual_risks: Independent bounded checks do not replace the analytic proof; scope limited to stated assumptions.
